summary: Hexagonal prompting: architecture as a prompt, a negative corpus that reached a class nothing had reached, static scanners removed, and an A/B decided by judged scorecards on a repaired instrument

assertions: Two arms exist as two prompt files; neither is the other with a section removed.
The seeded catalogue is a committed artifact with exact find/replace, a harness asserting each pattern occurs exactly once, and at least one fault in each mechanism's known gap.
PREDICTIONS-HP.md is committed before any other ticket is dispatched and contains at least three explicit NEGATIVE predictions.
acceptance.close_note: Assertion 1: two arms as two files, verified mechanically by `check_catalogue.py --arms` (neither prompt's line set is a subset of the other's). Arm B's HP-02 slot is DECLARED AND UNFILLED by design -- HP-01 does not write the treatment it is building the experiment to judge. Assertion 2: 10 mutants, every `find` proven to occur EXACTLY ONCE, apply/revert byte-identical, every mutant still parses, all four declared mechanism gaps seeded, plus one positive and one negative control. Assertion 3: PREDICTIONS-HP.md carries 7 positive and 6 NEGATIVE predictions, each with an ID, an instrument and a direction. Sealed before any other ticket is dispatched. MEASURED AND UNFLATTERING, recorded here rather than only in the fixture: the hand-written suite kills 10 of 10 mutants. That is the bar the generated corpus must clear, and if it scores lower HP-06 must say the generator is worse on this fixture than a suite written in an afternoon. One of HP-01's own 10 suite predictions (M02) was WRONG and was corrected before dispatch, with the error recorded beside it. Two findings FILED, not fixed: HP-01-DF-01 (the epic's own acceptance command is red at the epic tip, caused by the mandated worktree Skill Manager home shadowing basenames in test_source_citations.resolve_cited) and HP-01-DF-02 (the shipped EV-01 catalogue is rejected by the shipped kill_test parser over `effect_port` vs `port`).

tickets.objective: Build the experiment, then get out of the way. Three parts. (1) THE A/B TASK. One feature specification, written once, given to two agents: ARM A with an ordinary implementation prompt, ARM B with HP-02's hexagonal + minimize-complexity prompt. Same feature, same model, same seeded-fault catalogue, same judges. The arms are declared as two prompts in two files, never one prompt with a paragraph switched off, so a reader of the record can see which instrument produced which number. (2) THE SEEDED CATALOGUE, shipped as an artifact -- a `seeded_faults.toml`-shaped file with exact find/replace and a harness asserting each pattern occurs exactly once, so every number is re-derivable. Seed a fault IN THE GAP each mechanism is supposed to lose, including at least one guard-relaxation fault and one requiring a content assertion. A reduction result with no mutant in the gap is not a measurement. (3) COMMIT `examples/validation/PREDICTIONS-HP.md` BEFORE any other ticket is dispatched, with at least three NEGATIVE predictions -- what will NOT move. RP-02 is why: it closed a real oracle leak, took parameter recovery from 0 of 5 to 5 of 5, and moved the mutant matrix by zero cells. Nobody predicted that, and it killed a hypothesis recorded as fact. This ticket adds NO model surface. Per surface_cost_rule that is a feature.
tickets.title: The A/B harness, the scorecard baseline, and the sealed predictions

assertions: The prompt asks for ports and adapters and for the simplest behavior-preserving design, and instructs the agent to make NO check pass.
It ships as a prompt file; nothing in the toolchain refuses anything as a result of this ticket.
A worked example shows the prompt used end to end.
acceptance.close_note: Assertion 1: `prompts/hexagonal_implementation.md` asks for a domain that holds no handle/path/clock/env/network/global, a driven port the DOMAIN declares, a domain module that does not IMPORT its adapters, a working fake plus the identical case list against both, a named swap sentence, and an explicit prohibition on inventing ports for non-I/O. The simplicity half restates references/complexity_intuition.md's reading rules in code terms. NOT ONE NUMBER APPEARS IN THE ASK -- no threshold, no budget, no report to turn green -- and it names the round-2 duplication result and MF-020 explicitly. The same ask is inlined as arm B's Section 1 (HP-01's slot), which is the only edit made to examples/validation/. Assertion 2: two markdown files and one slot fill. Nothing in the toolchain reads them, no test enumerates them, and no checker was added -- including the "are the two copies still in sync" test that no_new_gates_rule forbids. `check_catalogue.py --arms` reports the slot FILLED; neither arm is a subset of the other. Assertion 3: worked end to end at specs/tickets/HP-02/results/pilot/ -- both arms dispatched verbatim to fresh agents against the shared FEATURE.md, both green on the shared suite (28 passed), the HP-01 catalogue re-anchored per arm with exactly-once and byte-identical revert proven per arm, and a per-class per-arm per-instrument kill table. THE LOCAL SIGNAL CAME BACK NEGATIVE ON TWO OF THREE GOALS, recorded here and not only in the evidence. GOAL-hexagonal-in-fact moved as expected (arm B: Protocol port, real adapter, working fake, one composition point, domain importing no I/O; arm A: none of them) -- but on my reading, not a judgement, at n=1, with the length confound now measured at 6.6x. GOAL-simpler-same-behavior moved THE WRONG WAY on the only available substitute (5 files / 274 lines against 1 / 120), reproducing the sealed N01, and its DECLARED instrument could not run at all (HP-02-DF-01). GOAL-catch-bugs, the guard, moved THE WRONG WAY BY ONE CELL: the shared suite is flat at 10/10 on both arms, but each arm's own tests scored A 4/10 against B 3/10 -- arm B wrote 3.6x the test code and caught one fault fewer -- and the arm-own instrument's positive control (M07) survives on BOTH arms, so by the catalogue's own P05 doctrine that row is not citeable as a kill measurement. AND THE PILOT FOUND A HOLE IN THE PROMPT ITSELF. Arm B's real-vs-fake test asserted `scenario(fake) == scenario(real)` -- two wirings of the SAME domain, so every domain-logic fault moves both sides identically and the test cannot fail for any fault in the rules. The artifact the prompt asked for, and that D3 anchor 4 is written about, was by construction blind to the faults D1 is about. One sentence was added to both copies of the ask afterwards; THE PILOT MEASURED THE TEXT BEFORE IT AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-RUN, so the shipped text is unmeasured and HP-06's A/B is its first measurement. Two findings FILED, not fixed: HP-02-DF-01 (the mechanical half of GOAL-simpler-same-behavior's harness has no runnable instrument on this fixture -- the scanner reads TLA+, both arms produce Python, and the one model is shared by design; three dispositions offered, the choice is the owner's) and HP-02-DF-02 (SKILL.md's index does not list the two new pages; deliberately left until HP-06 decides whether the prompt is worth pointing anyone at). PREDICTIONS-HP.md was not touched. Zero model surface added, per surface_cost_rule. WHERE THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS: `close ticket` consumes specs/tickets/HP-02/ into the append-only record, so every path listed above now reads specs/.history/hexagonal-prompting-epic/ticket-001-HP-02/ticket/results/. The `evidence:` paths are kept in the pre-close form for consistency with HP-01's entry, which has the same property.

tickets.objective: The architecture lever of this epic, and it is a PROMPT. Not a schema, not a check, not a gate. Owner direction 2026-08-03: the hoops already built are not smart enough to provide value and agents spend real time jumping through them, so architecture guidance moves into the ask. The hypothesis being tested, stated so it can fail: an agent working from the DIAGRAM -- far enough from the code that it is not defending existing structure -- will produce a modular, testable design if simply asked for one, and will preserve behavior while reducing complexity if told that is the goal. Build on what already ships: prompts/implementation_brief.md and prompts/aspect_decomposition.md (AC-03). The new prompt asks for ports and adapters explicitly -- a domain that does not import its I/O, driven ports behind interfaces, adapters swappable for fakes -- and asks for the SIMPLEST design that retains the behaviors, feeding the shipped complexity descriptor in AS GUIDANCE rather than gating on it. Two things the prompt must NOT do, both learned the hard way. It must not instruct the agent to make any check pass -- "make the coherence check clean" is a standing instruction to duplicate across component boundaries, measured in round 2. And it must not promise that a metric improving means the design improved: MF-020, a metric can improve because an edge was deleted.
tickets.title: The prompt: hexagonal architecture and minimize complexity, as instructions

assertions: A negative corpus emits, per reachable state, the disabled actions with the argument that would be refused, each asserting rejection.
Zero false rejections on the green control: no case asserts rejection of an input the model enables.
Byte-identical across two independent generations, INCLUDING its failing executions.
This model produces a corpus its own cap accepts, and the run states which projection made that true.
Per-class per-arm kill table reported. Never a single kill rate.
acceptance.close_note: THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME: guard relaxation moved off zero. 3 of 3 on HP-01's seeded catalogue and 5 of 5 on a fresh independently authored one, against 0 of 3 and 0 of 5 for the whole-view corpus on the same reference implementation and the same run. Baseline was 0 of 3, 0 of 3 and 0 of 4 across three catalogues, five instruments and two rounds. Assertion 1 MET. The mode evaluates each action's own body at every reachable state over every argument tuple its quantifier domains admit, and emits a case wherever it is definitely FALSE. 118 cases on the fixture, each carrying exact arguments and the violated conjunct verbatim as its rejection reason. Assertion 2 MET, and it is a property of the algorithm rather than of the fixture. Evaluation is three-valued; every unimplemented construct is UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN never emits, so an unsupported construct costs completeness and can never cost soundness. Cross-checked: 3,440 ENABLED edges re-evaluated at their own source states, 0 evaluated FALSE. The disabled set is computed by EVALUATING the model and never by subtracting the dump's edges -- measured, the dump holds 4,028 edges where 7,716 argument tuples are not disabled, so the subtraction would have reported enabled inputs as refusable. Assertion 3 MET including failing executions. Two full generations of a 43,246-case corpus (each with its own TLC run) are byte-identical across all six package files; two generations of the projected 541-case MCsmall corpus likewise; and two runs of the shipped runner over a corpus that FAILS 4 cases produce identical failure text, case order included. Assertion 4 PARTIALLY MET, and the shortfall is recorded rather than closed. `specs/current/tlc_projection.py` did not exist; it does now, and MCsmall goes from 3,678,217 cases / 7.4 GB (18,391x the cap) to 541 cases / 667 KB -- 6,799x -- by moving pure outputs and recorded verdicts out of the state into the asserted output, deleting no oracle. Every run now names its projection unprompted, in stdout and in docs.md. But 541 is still 2.7x the cap of 200, and HP-03 did NOT raise the cap: the accept path's suggested value is 541, the number this ticket produced, and a budget fitted to the result it must admit is not a budget. Filed HP-03-DF-02 for the owner. Assertion 5 PARTIALLY MET. Per-class per-instrument tables are reported for both catalogues with controls, and no aggregate rate is computed anywhere. The PER-ARM axis is NOT measurable at HP-03: the arms are implementations the A/B produces at HP-06 and neither has any code yet. Every number is on the fixture's reference implementation, which is explicitly not an arm. THE UNFLATTERING HALF, recorded here rather than only in the fixture. The hand-written suite kills 10 of 10. The whole-view corpus kills 5 of 10 and the two corpora together 8 of 10 -- so on this fixture the generator is still worse than a suite written in an afternoon, and HP-06 must say so. M07, a positive control the catalogue declares must die on every instrument on every arm, SURVIVES the whole-view corpus, because Reserve contributes zero executable cases. Only 3,440 of 43,128 positive cases (8.0%) are executable at all. THE COMPARISON THIS TICKET EXISTS TO MAKE. HP-01's fixture already contains the profile change -- seven explicit Refuse* actions. They produce 39,100 cases (90.7% of the corpus) carrying NO arguments, because their parameters appear nowhere in their bodies and no recovery mechanism can recover what the state pair does not contain. Zero of them are executable. The generator produces the same refusals as 118 executable cases. The negative corpus did not need a profile change; the profile change did not produce a usable negative corpus. ZERO MODEL SURFACE ADDED, per surface_cost_rule, argued rather than asserted in results/zero-model-delta.txt: a per-flag variant of the existing GenerateCases action, no new port, no second TLC run, 1x state space. Four findings FILED and none fixed. HP-03-DF-01 is the one worth reading: the fixture's model guards a reservation id its own API allocates rather than accepts, so 4 of 118 negative cases assert the rejection of a call the UNMUTATED reference correctly accepts. It is a true statement about a model that does not refine its own FEATURE.md, it was invisible to every existing instrument, and the negative corpus is what found it. HP-03-DF-04 retracts a documented limit: ordering is NOT invisible to corpora, it is invisible when the model represents the ordered thing as a set, and M09 died on the whole-view corpus because this model uses a sequence. WHERE THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS: `close ticket` consumes specs/tickets/HP-03/ into the append-only record, so every path above now reads specs/.history/hexagonal-prompting-epic/ticket-002-HP-03/ticket/results/. The measurement instruments -- the adapter, the fresh catalogue and the kill-table driver -- are sealed beside them under .../ticket/measure/. Reconciled onto epic tip 757de49 (schedule_revision 2, HP-02 merged). Re-checked HP-03's entry field by field against the amended plan: goals, contributions, expected effects, local signals, conflict keys, wave, promotion order and predecessor are all unchanged by the amendment, which touched only GOAL-simpler-same-behavior's metric and harness.

tickets.objective: The single largest available increase in what a generated corpus can see, and the only ticket aimed at a fault class that has measured ZERO on every instrument in every round. A generated corpus replays only ENABLED edges, so it contains no rejected inputs: a service that accepts what the model forbids passes every case. Round 1: 0 of 3. Round 2: 0 of 3, on both arms, AFTER RP-02 took parameter recovery from 0 of 5 to 5 of 5 -- which moved nothing and thereby falsified round 1's own explanation. RP-02 counted why: all 330 recovered arguments are arguments the guard ACCEPTS, 0 are rejected inputs, and 220 refusable pairs exist in the state space a state graph can never emit. A third blind catalogue reproduced it unaided: `330 'status': 'applied'` -- the corpus never once asks the program to reject a call. So build the generator mode: at each reachable state, the actions whose guards are DISABLED, emitted as cases asserting the call is REJECTED. TLC already knows them; the profile does not widen. AND MAKE A CORPUS TRACTABLE, because today one is not. Carries RC-02-DF-04 and MF026-R4-F-01: `generate cases` on MCsmall -- the config that exists to make a corpus tractable -- produces 3,678,217 cases and a 7.4 GB file CPython cannot import, 18,391x the manifest's own cap, and this model has no tlc_projection.py while every worked example does. A negative corpus nobody can run is not a mechanism. DO NOT BUDGET ANY OF THIS AGAINST PARAMETER RECOVERY. That hypothesis is dead, measured, and retracted in writing.
tickets.title: The negative corpus: TLC's disabled edges, asserted rejected -- and a corpus that fits its own cap

assertions: The oracle loads the adapters of a freshly scaffolded project without the caller adjusting sys.path.
An adapter that cannot execute a case is SKIPPED AND REPORTED, never aborting the run.
Two runs over an identical corpus report an identical gap count. A nondeterministic oracle is a finding, however good its first run.
A slice narrower than its view runs end to end with no owner writing the author a file, and any derived mapping states which oracles it does NOT carry.
acceptance.close_note: ALL FOUR ASSERTIONS MET, AND THE HEADLINE RESULT IS THE ONE HP-01 PREDICTED WOULD BE UNFLATTERING: THE MUTANT MATRIX MOVED BY ZERO CELLS. Assertion 1: `run effect-conformance --target specs/current` runs with no PYTHONPATH. Also demonstrated on a project this CLI freshly scaffolded (scaffolded-project.txt), whose mapping uses a different convention again -- `specs.program_model.adapters:X` rather than the bare `production_adapters:X` this repository uses. Both resolve. Assertion 2: the oracle reports on 18 of 18 modeled actions and DRIVES 8.
